name: Wireless & Cellular Security
description: Security of cellular (4G/5G), Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS, and other RF/wireless protocols.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area (2018) staked out two enduring themes: attacks on the physical-layer signals that wireless systems trust, and the security of the embedded devices that ride on them. "All Your GPS Are Belong To Us: Towards Stealthy Manipulation of Road Navigation Systems" (2018) showed that GPS spoofing could be made subtle enough to quietly reroute drivers, while "Off-Path TCP Exploit: How Wireless Routers Can Jeopardize Your Secrets" (2018) found a timing side channel baked into the half-duplex nature of Wi-Fi itself. In parallel, "ACES: Automatic Compartments for Embedded Systems" (2018) reflected growing worry about the bare-metal IoT devices that increasingly sit at the edge of wireless networks.

By 2019-2020 the focus sharpened onto the cellular and short-range standards everyone depends on. "Hiding in Plain Signal: Physical Signal Overshadowing Attack on LTE" (2019) and "Call Me Maybe: Eavesdropping Encrypted LTE Calls With ReVoLTE" (2020) demonstrated that LTE's control and voice planes could be manipulated or decrypted, while "The KNOB is Broken: Exploiting Low Entropy in the Encryption Key Negotiation Of Bluetooth BR/EDR" (2019) exposed a foundational weakness in the Bluetooth pairing standard. A second strand turned to finding bugs at scale: "Frankenstein: Advanced Wireless Fuzzing to Exploit New Bluetooth Escalation Targets" (2020) pioneered emulation-based fuzzing of real Bluetooth firmware.

The 2021-2022 era is defined by systematic, tooling-driven security analysis and a maturing privacy threat model. Negative-testing and directed-fuzzing frameworks like "DoLTEst: In-depth Downlink Negative Testing Framework for LTE Devices" (2022) and "BrakTooth: Causing Havoc on Bluetooth Link Manager via Directed Fuzzing" (2022) made vulnerability discovery repeatable across many devices, and privacy attacks such as "Watching the Watchers: Practical Video Identification Attack in LTE Networks" (2022) showed encrypted cellular traffic still leaks what users are doing. GPS work also moved from theory to the field with "An Experimental Study of GPS Spoofing and Takeover Attacks on UAVs" (2022).

Most recently (2023-2024) the area leans heavily on formal methods and automated reasoning over protocol specifications, plus surprising new side channels. "Sherlock on Specs: Building LTE Conformance Tests through Automated Reasoning" (2023), "BASECOMP: A Comparative Analysis for Integrity Protection in Cellular Baseband Software" (2023), and "Logic Gone Astray: A Security Analysis Framework for the Control Plane Protocols of 5G Basebands" (2024) push security analysis up into the baseband and the 5G control plane, while "Framing Frames: Bypassing Wi-Fi Encryption by Manipulating Transmit Queues" (2023) and "Eavesdropping Mobile App Activity via Radio-Frequency Energy Harvesting" (2023) prove that even mature, widely deployed RF technologies keep yielding new attack surfaces.

milestones.title: All Your GPS Are Belong To Us: Towards Stealthy Manipulation of Road Navigation Systems
milestones.note: made GPS spoofing stealthy enough to covertly mislead real navigation, setting the agenda for RF positioning attacks

milestones.title: Hiding in Plain Signal: Physical Signal Overshadowing Attack on LTE
milestones.note: showed LTE's open medium lets attackers overshadow legitimate signals, opening up cellular control-plane attacks

milestones.title: The KNOB is Broken: Exploiting Low Entropy in the Encryption Key Negotiation Of Bluetooth BR/EDR
milestones.note: exposed a standard-level flaw in Bluetooth key negotiation affecting essentially every device

milestones.title: Call Me Maybe: Eavesdropping Encrypted LTE Calls With ReVoLTE
milestones.note: decrypted encrypted VoLTE calls, a high-impact break of deployed cellular voice security

milestones.title: BrakTooth: Causing Havoc on Bluetooth Link Manager via Directed Fuzzing
milestones.note: scaled directed fuzzing to systematically uncover implementation bugs across many Bluetooth chipsets

milestones.title: Framing Frames: Bypassing Wi-Fi Encryption by Manipulating Transmit Queues
milestones.note: bypassed Wi-Fi encryption via queue manipulation, proving mature Wi-Fi still has design-level weaknesses

milestones.title: Logic Gone Astray: A Security Analysis Framework for the Control Plane Protocols of 5G Basebands
milestones.note: brought automated differential analysis to 5G baseband control-plane logic, marking the move into 5G
